name: Cat Ba food guide
summary: After the boat you eat from the harbor: seafood by weight on đường 1/4 and đường Núi Ngọc, plus forest honey, Liên Minh chicken, a Gia Luận orange, Hiền Hào taro, and Cát Hải fish sauce.
body: Come back from Lan Ha hungry. The meal to ask for is cá song, bề bề, tu hài, ngao Phù Long, gà Liên Minh, mật ong rừng, cam Gia Luận, khoai sọ Hiền Hào, and nước mắm Cát Hải.
Island seafood is at its best in winter, before the spring spawn, with rượu mật ong or rượu hồng hoa in the glass.
On đường 1/4 and đường Núi Ngọc you choose the rest by weight, by the plate, by the pair, or by the piece. Skip a kitchen that will not post its prices, or that changes a posted price.
Take home mật ong Cát Bà, dark yellow, thick, and fragrant, from the households that keep the bees, and a bottle of nước mắm Cát Hải from the neighboring island.
specialtiesLead: The nine island foods first, then the seafood, porridges, and noodle bowls of the harbor streets.

sections.heading: City specialties
paragraphs: Cá song, bề bề, tu hài, ngao Phù Long, gà Liên Minh, mật ong rừng, cam Gia Luận, khoai sọ Hiền Hào, and nước mắm Cát Hải lead the list. After them come the prawns, fish, crabs, shellfish, and snails the harbor kitchens sell by weight, with the size grades folded into each name.

Ngao hấp xả, gà nướng mật ong, cá thu kho một nắng, cháo ngao, cháo cá, bánh đa cua, and phở are prepared plates and bowls. Everything else you choose by weight, by the plate, by the pair, or by the piece.

sections.heading: The harbor streets
paragraphs: After the boat, eat on đường 1/4 in Cát Bà town, where the seafood kitchens sell by weight. Đường Núi Ngọc, the phố ẩm thực, is the second food street. One address writes that food street in thị trấn Cát Hải.
Bến Bèo has the quay kitchens, at tổ 11 in Cát Bà town, 1.5 km from the town center, or about 2 km by road.
Cổng chợ Cát Bà, the market gate, is the address of two more seafood kitchens, one without a town name and one in thị trấn Cát Hải. After dinner, the town’s night market sells sea souvenirs.
Floating kitchens sit on vịnh Cảng Cá, the old fish-port bay in town, and on vịnh Cái Bèo. The working fish port moved to cảng cá Trân Châu on 10 November 2021.
Out on vịnh Lan Hạ, the floating market is smaller than a Mekong one and is mostly the fish-raft keepers. You can buy seafood there to take home as a gift.

seoTitle: Cat Ba food guide — seafood after the Lan Ha boat
seoDescription: Seafood by weight on đường 1/4 and Núi Ngọc after the boat, from cá song and bề bề to forest honey and Cát Hải fish sauce.
